rounds.diagnosis: State-conditional self-model anchors fixed C3 completely: idle P(stay) = 1.0 for both low and high (raw mean daily steps: high idle 7,931, low idle 2,929, vs round-1 high-idle collapse to moderate). C5 also holds cleanly (high 1.0 vs 1.0, low 0.0 vs 0.0). C4 regressed on the surface (0/4 vs 1/4) for a structural reason: with persistence fixed, idle P(high) = 1.0 in high states so ability_morning cannot raise it, and low states anchored at ~3,000 cannot cross the >7,000 threshold even with the boost (raw intervention boost landed at ~+110-120, below the +150-450 guidance). C4 can only pass for states where idle P(high) is near 0 and the intervention day crosses 7,000 (moderate-band cells anchored ~6,600-6,800), which the pilot subset omits. C6 still fails on morning_steps_ratio (52/52 cells balanced): the subset pins the factor to balanced and the model now faithfully respects the state, so the check cannot pass without varying that factor in the state subset.
next_steps: Round 3 (com_b_mechanisms): strengthen intervention effect magnitude so the boost reliably lands in +150-450 (raw mean ~+110-120)

For C4 signal, extend the pilot state subset to include moderate recent_steps_mean cells (6 states x 13 actions x 3 = 234 calls) or evaluate sensitivity on a continuous step shift (needs analyzer change)
For C6, vary morning_steps_ratio / walk_pattern / day_of_week in the pilot subset so the time-of-day share guidance can manifest

diagnosis: Mechanism framing strengthened the intervention response on average but unevenly. Overall mean lift rose to +149.6 steps/day (round 2: +115), at the lower edge of the +150-450 target, with 31/48 cells positive; distribution is wide (min -228.6, max +1,036.4). Per state: high/major idle 6,864 -> lift +382.4 (in band); low/none idle 3,514 -> +112.5; low/major idle 3,388 -> +97.5 (still under target); high/none idle 7,210 -> +6.2. The near-zero high/none lift suggests the model applied the causal rule literally: a high-activity, no-burden person was judged to have no barriers, so every nudge was treated as unmatched -> negligible, instead of the persona (moderate barriers everywhere) making all nudges matched. C3 regressed (high idle P(stay) 1.0 -> 0.333; high idle means drifted to 7,210/6,864, straddling the 7,000 bin threshold, vs 7,931/7,960 in round 2): the compact persistence clause is weaker than round 2's explicit numeric anchor (~8,000 +/-500), which should be kept in future variants. C2 failed for the first time (51/52): 8/156 responses had malformed day JSON (quote typo on one line), concentrated in major-burden morning cells, and one cell lost 2 samples. C4 shows its first real signal (1/4, dP=+0.667 in high/major) precisely because persistence weakened there, freeing headroom; still structural in the other 3 cells. C5 holds (high 0.795 -> 0.667, low 0.0 -> 0.0). C6 remains structural in this subset (morning_ratio balanced in 49/51 cells).
next_steps: Round 4 (empirical_anchors): keep the mechanism framing but restore round-2-style explicit numeric state anchors (low ~3,000 / moderate ~5,500 / high ~8,000, +/-500) to recover C3; pair the causal rule with a stated barriers profile per state so matched/unmatched is unambiguous
Reinforce JSON-format adherence (the 8 malformed responses) e.g. by re-stating 'one JSON object per line, no trailing characters' in the format instruction
For C4 signal, extend the pilot subset to moderate recent_steps_mean cells (234 calls) or evaluate sensitivity on a continuous step shift (analyzer change)
For C6, vary morning_steps_ratio / walk_pattern / day_of_week in the pilot subset

rounds.prompt_changes_since_previous: Added system_extra combining three blocks: (a) NUMERIC ANCHORS restored from round 2 (low = under 4,000 / moderate = 4,000-7,000 / high = over 7,000 daily steps; without intervention the person stays at their level - high around 8,000, low around 3,000; 'On days with no intervention (idle), the person simply continues at their own established level; never regress a stated high or low person toward the population average'); (b) BARRIER PROFILE naming one of four profiles per (recent_steps_mean, burden) cell - low/none = struggling walker, effort/self-efficacy barrier; low/major = struggling walker under strain, fatigue AND opportunity barriers; high/none = active person, complacency and reinforcement barriers; high/major = active person under strain, scheduling/fatigue (NOT capability) barrier - with the statement that every profile has at least one real barrier and a matched nudge relieves it; (c) CAUSAL RULE kept from round 3 (matched nudge = +150-450 steps that day, target the middle of the band ~+300; unmatched = small or negligible) plus the EMPIRICAL ANCHOR from the PEARL paper (ability/technique messages most effective and best received, 90% thumbs-up, followed by perceived benefit; planning and prioritization help specifically when major burden interferes with acting). action_overrides copies round 3's 12 mechanism sentences verbatim and appends one matched-clause per sentence ('It is a matched nudge for anyone whose ... is the barrier'); idle unchanged. user_extra is a callable returning per-state BARRIER PROFILE TODAY line naming the profile from (b) plus the matched-nudge ~150-450 steps rule; returns '' on idle so nothing renders.

diagnosis: Combining numeric anchors + barrier profiles + mechanisms restored C3 in the aggregate (idle P(stay) low 1.0 / high 0.5 - exactly at the 0.5 threshold): high/none idle climbed back from round 3's 7,210 to 7,554 (in band, above the 7,000 bin), but high/major idle is still 6,871 (vs 6,864 in round 3) - below the 7,000 threshold, so that cell still bins moderate (P(high)=0.0) and the check passes only because high/none carries it. The 'graded down under major burden' language appears to counteract the 'stay around 8,000' anchor for the major-burden cell.

The barrier profile made the matched/unmatched classification too strict and destroyed the lift: overall mean lift +43.1 steps/day (round 3: +149.6, round 2: +115), only 26/48 cells positive (round 3: 31/48), min -547.6 / max +1,219.0. With only 1-2 named barriers per profile, the model judges 8-10 of the 12 themes unmatched per state and outputs near-idle days; at temp 0.7 that no-op distribution swings negative (low/major -195.1, high/none -138.2). The few judged-matched cells overshoot badly (planning_afternoon +1,219, social_opportunity_afternoon +960, physical_opportunity_morning +745 in high/major), far above the +450 cap.

high/none is still the worst cell (mean lift -138.2, vs +6.2 in round 3): naming 'complacency and reinforcement' as the barriers did not give the model a concrete lever to act on - every theme is treated as unmatched again, just recoded from round 3's 'no barriers'. The binary matched/unmatched rule, applied per-profile with 12 themes but 1-2 barriers, is incompatible with the aggregate +150-450 target.

2/156 malformed-JSON responses (quote typo class, both morning cells) - down from 8 in round 3, no cell lost. C4 shows 1/4 again (dP=+1.0 in high/major, where idle P(high)=0.0 leaves headroom); C5 passes (high 0.872 -> 0.718); C6 remains structural in this subset (morning_ratio balanced in 52/52 cells).
next_steps: Round 5 (protocol): either make the barrier profile grade matched-nudge strength instead of switching matchedness off (all 12 themes produce +150-450 for every profile, with the stated barrier themes toward the top of the band), or make unmatched nudges produce a small guaranteed floor (+0-100) instead of 'negligible' so the mean of matched+unmatched stays in band

Fix high/major persistence: the burden tier must modulate the intervention boost, not the idle baseline - state explicitly that idle stays at the person's own level REGARDLESS of burden, and move the burden grading to lift size only
For C4 signal, extend the pilot subset to moderate recent_steps_mean cells (234 calls) or evaluate sensitivity on a continuous step shift (analyzer change)
For C6, vary morning_steps_ratio / walk_pattern / day_of_week in the pilot subset
Keep hardening the JSON format instruction (2 malformed responses this round, both morning cells)
